requirements.text: Use Vite + React + TypeScript with react-router for the project.
Style the site with plain CSS using a design‑token theme implemented as CSS custom properties.
`npm run build` must produce a `dist/index.html` file.
The site must be a static site with no backend, no user accounts, no analytics, no third‑party scripts, and no external font or image CDNs.
Use the color palette deep navy (#0B1F3A) as primary, white as background, and teal (#1F8A8A) as accent.
Apply a serif system‑font stack for headings and a clean sans‑serif system‑font stack for body text.
Display an inline‑SVG wordmark logo consisting of a small bell‑curve graphic followed by the text "The Bayes Group".
The layout must be responsive from 390 px width (phone) to 1440 px width (desktop) and never scroll horizontally.
On phones the header navigation must collapse into a "Menu" button that toggles the visibility of the navigation links.
Header on every page must contain the wordmark linking to "/", navigation links to Services, Training, About, Contact, and a "Book a consultation" button linking to "/contact".
Footer on every page must contain the wordmark, the line "AI enablement, training and custom development.", the same navigation links as the header, and the text "© 2026 The Bayes Group".
Each page must set its document.title correctly (e.g., "Services | The Bayes Group" for /services and "The Bayes Group | Evidence-driven AI" for the home page).
Each page must contain exactly one <h1> element.
Home page hero must display an <h1> with text "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business.".
Home page hero must contain a sentence of value proposition and two buttons: "Book a consultation" linking to /contact and "Explore services" linking to /services.

Home page must show three pillar cards titled "AI Enablement", "Training" and "Custom Development" each with two or three sentences and a "Learn more" link to the corresponding section on /services (/services#enablement, /services#training, /services#custom-development).
Home page must have a "How we work" section with four numbered steps: Assess, Design, Build, Enable, each step showing one sentence.
Home page must have a "Why The Bayes Group" section with four points: credentialed data scientists, hands‑on builders, vendor‑neutral advice, knowledge transfer so your team owns the result.
Home page must end with a call‑to‑action band containing the text "Ready to put AI to work?" and a "Book a consultation" button.
Services page must have an <h1> with text "Services".
Services page must contain three sections with ids "enablement", "training", and "custom-development" in that order.
Enablement section must list: AI readiness assessment; use‑case discovery and prioritization; AI strategy and roadmap; AI governance and responsible‑AI policy.
Training section must list: executive AI briefings; hands‑on team workshops; deep‑learning bootcamps for technical teams; custom curricula.

Custom development section must list: LLM and retrieval‑augmented (RAG) applications; AI agents and workflow automation; predictive models and ML pipelines; deep‑learning solutions; integration with existing systems.
Each listed item on the Services page must show its name and a one‑sentence description.
Each Services section must end with a line "Typical engagement: 2 to 6 weeks" (example wording).
Training page must have an <h1> with text "Training".
Training page must display at least six course cards.

Each course card must show the course title, audience (exactly one of: Executives, Managers, Technical teams), format (Half‑day briefing, 1‑day workshop or Multi‑week bootcamp), duration, and a "You will learn" list of three items.
At least one course must exist for each audience type (Executives, Managers, Technical teams).
Above the catalog on the Training page must be four filter buttons labeled All, Executives, Managers, Technical teams.
When the page loads, the "All" filter button must be selected and all courses must be visible.
Clicking a filter button for an audience must show only the courses whose audience matches that filter.
The selected filter button must be visually distinguished and have aria-pressed="true".
About page must have an <h1> with text "About".
About page must contain a mission paragraph and a "Why Bayes" paragraph describing Bayesian reasoning as the approach.
About page must include two founder cards with placeholder content: name "Founder Name", role "Co‑founder & Principal Data Scientist", a credentials list and a short bio, all marked as placeholders.
About page must list four values: Evidence over hype; Build to transfer; Vendor‑neutral; Responsible by design.
Contact page must have an <h1> with text "Book a consultation".
Contact page must display the email address hello@thebayesgroup.com.
Contact page must contain a form with labelled fields: Name, Email, Company, "What can we help with?" (select with options AI Enablement, Training, Custom Development, Not sure yet), and Message.
Name, Email and Message fields are required.
Email field must validate that the input is a syntactically valid email address.

When a required field is empty or Email is invalid on submit, an error message must appear next to the field: "Please enter your name.", "Please enter a valid email address.", or "Please enter a message." respectively.
On an invalid submit, no network request must be sent.
On a valid submit, no network request is sent; the UI must display the message "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day." and clear all form fields.
Any unknown route must render a page with an <h1> "Page not found" and a link back to the home page.
All pages must include semantic landmarks: <header>, <nav>, <main>, and <footer>.
Every form field must have an associated <label> element.
Keyboard focus outline must be visible on interactive elements.
All text must meet WCAG AA contrast requirements against its background.

R12.test: sets correct document title and contains a single h1

R32.test: filter buttons exist, All is selected by default, and have correct aria-pressed values

R33.test: Audience filter works: only courses for the selected audience are displayed

R42.test: validation errors appear when required fields are missing or email is invalid

R43.test: validation errors appear when required fields are missing or email is invalid
R43.quote: expect(screen.getByText('Please enter a valid email address.')).toBeInTheDocument();
R43.gap: (claimed test quote not found in the file)

R45.gap: No test verifies that a network request is not sent on an invalid submit.

R46.test: successful submission shows thank‑you message, clears the form, and makes no network request
